answer: Verifying is deliberately cheaper than producing, and that asymmetry is the whole design: a juror can walk a claim to its weakest vertex in a minute, while writing a defensible one takes a real attempt. A farm pays production cost on every head, but the network spends almost nothing to reject them, so the exchange rate runs against the attacker. Prose that wanders through a karst of caveats never states what would falsify it, and a claim with no falsifier is exactly what a grader is trained to mark down.
